overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to respond within 10 days to a minutes request and by not reviewing executive session minutes for release within 30 days; no intent finding, but a warning.

allegations.summary: Complainant requested February 1 meeting minutes (mostly executive session) on April 14, treated by the Board as a records request; no response within 10 days.
allegations.key_passage: By failing to provide any response within 10 calendar days, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not review executive session minutes for release, or provide them, within 30 days of the request, as the second complaint restated.
allegations.key_passage: The Board did not review the minutes to determine whether they could be released to the public until May 30, which was its fifth meeting and more than 30 days following the request, and therefore violated the Open Meeting Law in this additional respect.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements for responding to requests for meeting minutes, including executive session minutes.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
